Thanks Ben — attaching a draft narrative (verdant-tailored-narrative.docx) and the redacted PDF. Summary below that I suggest we send straight to Verdant as the top-of-binder narrative. Please review for anything missing.

Draft narrative (summary):
Redwood Inference maintains a strict separation between the control plane and customer data planes across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. The control plane (management APIs, configuration, model catalog, and scheduling) runs on isolated management clusters using separate VPCs/subnets and distinct IAM principals. Customer inference workloads run in tenant-specific compute pools (Dedicated GPU pools or customer-managed Private clusters) with no inbound management-plane access; control-plane actions are executed through authenticated, audited RPCs over mutually authenticated channels.

For Dedicated deployments we enforce network ACLs and subnet-level isolation between tenant compute pools and shared services; a tiered firewall model (edge / service / control) restricts east-west lateral movement. Private deployments follow the customer's network controls but leverage an "airlock proxy" for third-party integrations and outbound telemetry; the proxy enforces hostname allowlists and TLS inspection at the boundary.

Attached evidence: redacted topology (control_plane_fence_v1.pdf), ACL matrix (network_acl_matrix.xlsx), and this narrative document. All artifacts are prepared for inclusion in a SOC 2 binder and have been redacted to remove tenant-specific IPs and keys.

Leah / SOC2 team — attaching the requested artifacts for your binder. Per Verdant's ask, this package includes a short narrative, a redacted topology PDF, and an ACL matrix. Highlights below:  

1) Control-plane separation: Control plane components are deployed to a management VPC with no direct inbound access into tenant compute pools. All control operations are executed over authenticated RPCs and are recorded in immutable audit logs.
2) Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated uses Redwood-managed GPU pools with tenancy fencing enforced via subnet isolation and ACLs; Private uses customer-managed compute where Redwood's control plane communicates over mutual TLS and the customer's approved network path.
3) Airlock / outbound controls: For Private deployments, an optional airlock proxy mediates outbound third-party connections; the proxy does hostname allowlisting and records outbound requests to the audit stream.

Attachments included: control_plane_fence_v1.pdf (redacted network diagram), network_acl_matrix.xlsx (service ACLs), verdant-tailored-narrative.docx (narrative).
